title: README troubleshooting cites two non-existent error codes (`NotSignedIn 9101`, `TicketExpired 9103`) that operators will never see in the wire
userImpact: When an operator's 24h ticket expires and they grep the README for the error code they actually got, they find nothing. README troubleshooting tells them to expect `NotSignedIn (9101)` or `TicketExpired (9103)`. The actual production code throws either raw `NotSignedIn (203)` (SDK code) or synthetic `LoginExpired (9007)`. Code 9101 (`ReAuthRequired`) is defined but never thrown by anything in production. Code 9103 is `InvalidAppId`, NOT `TicketExpired` â€” and `TicketExpired` is a status name that doesn't exist in SyntheticStatusCodes at all. So the wire fingerprint the README documents simply cannot occur; the troubleshooting section is unreachable.
description: Grep across .md files shows ARCHITECTURE.md lines 34/62/79/111 all describe expiry as "synth 9101 with remediation". README.md:291 escalates by naming `TicketExpired (9103)` â€” but SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:87 defines 9103 as `InvalidAppId` (P15-007). The only code actually thrown on expiry is `LoginExpired (9007)` per LacerteSessionManager.cs:1369 (`ThrowIfAuthExpired`). And LoginCommand.cs:74 prints to operator stderr: "tools will return TicketExpired (9103) once the current ticket lapses" â€” also wrong, will mislead anyone trying to triage.
recommendation: Either (a) wire `ReAuthRequired (9101)` actually into ThrowIfAuthExpired and the AutoReconnect NotSignedIn path so the docs become true, or (b) rewrite all five doc/code sites to say `LoginExpired (9007)` and `NotSignedIn (203 sdk)` â€” which is what really fires. Option (b) is the smaller change. Also delete the `TicketExpired (9103)` reference everywhere it appears (no such name exists). After the fix, run `grep -nE "9101|9103|TicketExpired"` across .md and CLI commands and confirm only intended results remain.
rationale: Cross-checked SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:27-102 (codes 9007=LoginExpired, 9101=ReAuthRequired-never-thrown, 9103=InvalidAppId) against LacerteSessionManager.cs:1364-1369 (ThrowIfAuthExpired throws LoginExpired). No throw site for 9101 in production code (only in tests at LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:51). `TicketExpired` is not a defined symbol anywhere.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified all five cited sites. The drift is real and induced by prior round-2 work, never reconciled:

(1) README.md:291 â€” Says expired sessions surface as `NotSignedIn (9101)` or `TicketExpired (9103)`. Wrong on both counts: `NotSignedIn` is SDK code 203 (not 9101); 9101 is `ReAuthRequired` and is NEVER thrown in production (Grep across src finds only one use, in LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:51). `TicketExpired` is not a defined StatusInfo name anywhere â€” 9103 is `InvalidAppId` per SyntheticStatusCodes.cs:87/201, the slot allocated by P15-007 to fix the mis-categorized AppNotRegistered throw. The actual production code thrown on 24h expiry is `LoginExpired (9007)` per LacerteSessionManager.cs:1369 ThrowIfAuthExpired (wired by P15-043).

(2) LoginCommand.cs:74 â€” Prints to operator stderr: 'tools will return TicketExpired (9103) once the current ticket lapses'. This string was implanted verbatim by the P15-028 round-2 refinedRecommendation (audit-findings-r2.json:681), which suggested the wording before P15-007 had finalized 9103=InvalidAppId. The two round-2 verdicts collided and no doc-reconciliation pass caught it.

(3) ARCHITECTURE.md lines 34, 62, 79, 111 â€” All four describe expiry remediation as 'synth 9101'. Line 111 says 'every tool call short-circuits to synthetic 9101 with remediation pointing to lacerte-mcp login'. Line 79 (Boundary Invariant #8) makes the same claim. Production wires `LoginExpired (9007)` for the proactive probe; the reactive NotSignedIn path through AutoReconnect.cs explicitly propagates unchanged (line 194: 'LacerteSDKError carries a TAPIStatus â€” those are NEVER transient'), so an operator hitting reactive expiry sees raw SDK code 203, never 9101.

(4) REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:126 â€” Asserts 'every tool call short-circuits to synthetic 9101 ReAuthRequired with the lacerte-mcp login remediation message'. This is a regression test the operator can never pass because nothing throws 9101.

Not a duplicate of prior rounds: P15-007 added 9103=InvalidAppId (didn't audit existing 9103 mentions). P15-028 added the LoginCommand stderr line (using the now-wrong code). P15-043 wired LoginExpired=9007 as the actual expiry throw site (didn't update the docs that still cited 9101). The integration gap between the three is what this finding catches.

User-experience cost is concrete: a tax pro at 9am the next day sees `{statusCode: 9007, statusName: "LoginExpired"}` in the wire, greps the README for '9007' (finds nothing), then for 'LoginExpired' (finds nothing in README), then reads the troubleshooting section verbatim and is told to expect a code they're not seeing. Trust in docs erodes; triage time grows. LLM clients have the same problem â€” Claude Desktop showing 9007 to the model while the README it's been pointed at advertises 9101/9103 makes the LLM less likely to map to the correct remediation.

Recommendation is small and high-leverage (option b in the finding): five edits to align docs with what actually fires. Sim-only, no Lacerte SDK needed, can be locked with a single regression test that greps the .md files for the right symbols.

Slight over-statement in the finding: 9101 and 9103 ARE defined constants, just not what the docs imply. But the user impact is identical â€” operators searching for codes they actually see will not find a match.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Single pass to reconcile docs with the codes that actually fire. Five edits + one regression test.

(1) README.md:289-293 â€” Rewrite the symptom + diagnosis block to:
'**Symptom:** Reads + writes that worked yesterday now fail with status `LoginExpired (9007)` (proactive probe) or raw SDK `NotSignedIn (203)` (if the reactive NotSignedIn slips past the probe). Both error envelopes include the remediation `Run lacerte_register to re-authenticate (consent is one-time; only the sign-in needs refresh).`'
This makes the README the canonical fingerprint that matches what operators actually see in tool envelopes.

(2) LoginCommand.cs:74 â€” Change the stderr line to:
`Console.Error.WriteLine("          Existing 24h ticket cannot be renewed until upgrade â€” tools will return LoginExpired (9007) once the current ticket lapses.");`
Mirror the same correction in the comment at line 71.

(3) ARCHITECTURE.md:111 â€” Change 'short-circuits to synthetic 9101' to 'short-circuits to synthetic 9007 (LoginExpired) via the ThrowIfAuthExpired probe in LacerteSessionManager'. Cross-reference DECISIONS.md if a 'Auth expiry surfacing code' entry exists; if not, add one.

(4) ARCHITECTURE.md:34 â€” Update the diagram comment `- Idempotency cache (synth 9101 reuse)` â€” this is wrong twice over. 9101 isn't idempotency, 9102 is (IdempotencyConflict). Fix to: `- Idempotency cache (synth 9102 conflict)`.

(5) ARCHITECTURE.md:62 + :79 â€” Both reference '9101' in the resilience / Boundary Invariant #8 context. Change 9101 to '9007 (proactive probe) and raw 203 NotSignedIn (reactive path; AutoReconnect propagates unchanged per Resilience/AutoReconnect.cs:194)'. The invariant text should be honest that the reactive path is currently raw.

(6) REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md:126 â€” Change to: 'After 24h elapse OR explicit logout: every tool call that touches RequireContext short-circuits to synthetic 9007 LoginExpired with the `lacerte_register` remediation message; calls that bypass RequireContext (e.g. lacerte_session_status) still succeed and report registered:false.' This matches the actual P15-043 implementation.

(7) Decide what to do with 9101 ReAuthRequired (currently a dead constant). Two options:
  (a) Delete it from SyntheticStatusCodes.cs + StatusTable + LacerteSDKErrorTests.cs:51 â€” it's a docs-promised behavior that was never built and no longer planned (9007 covers the use case).
  (b) Wire it into AutoReconnect's NotSignedIn detection path so the reactive case finally surfaces a friendly code instead of raw 203. This is more work but closes Boundary Invariant #8 honestly. The P15-043 verdict explicitly suggested this as a follow-up.
Recommend (a) for this round; track (b) as a separate Todo. Reasoning: a dead constant that docs falsely reference is worse than no constant â€” operators reading SyntheticStatusCodes.cs will see 9101 ReAuthRequired and assume something throws it.

(8) Regression test â€” add `src/LacertMCP.Tests/Docs/StatusCodeDocsAlignmentTests.cs` with one test per doc file:
- Asserts README.md does NOT contain the substrings `9101`, `9103`, or `TicketExpired` (after the fix, these strings must not appear because they're wrong or refer to InvalidAppId which is not an auth-lifecycle thing).
- Asserts ARCHITECTURE.md does NOT contain `9101` (after delete + fix).
- Asserts REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md does NOT contain `9101 ReAuthRequired`.
- Asserts LoginCommand.cs does NOT contain `TicketExpired`.
- Asserts the codes that DO appear in StatusInfo.cs StatusTable are referenced at least once in README.md (catches future drift the other direction).

Verify with `Grep -nE "9101|9103|TicketExpired|ReAuthRequired" --glob "*.md"` post-edit; only the SyntheticStatusCodes.cs definition of 9103=InvalidAppId should remain (and only if option (a) above is chosen, no 9101 anywhere).

title: README claims `register` calls ITPRegistration.Register(); actual code returns exit 3 with '[partial] not yet wired'
userImpact: A tax pro follows the README's setup ceremony step 4, runs `lacerte-mcp register --app-name "Operator Lacerte MCP" --tax-year 2024`, sees the GUID print, exit-code 3, and a `[partial]` message on stderr saying the Intuit consent ceremony is not actually wired. README never warns them. They will assume their install is broken, file a bug, or worse â€” set LACERTE_LIVE=1 in Claude Desktop and discover at first tool call that nothing works.
description: README line 117 promises `register` 'Mints an AppID GUID, persists it to Windows Credential Manager, calls `ITPRegistration.Register()`, and prints the GUID for backup.' Line 230 repeats: 'on Windows + live SDK calls `ITPRegistration.Register(...)` which surfaces the consent + Intuit dialogs to the interactive shell.' Line 286-287 troubleshoots 'register opened no dialog' by telling the operator to switch to an interactive PowerShell â€” but no shell change will help, because `RegisterCommand.InvokeLiveRegister` (line 111-114) writes `[partial] AppID minted, but the Intuit consent ceremony is not yet wired into the CLI (Phase 9 task #63)` and returns exit 3. `LoginCommand.Run` (line 73-75) is identical. Same goes for the troubleshooting section's `lacerte-mcp login` 24h-refresh fix (line 293) â€” login is also stubbed. The README sells a complete onboarding flow that the code explicitly is not delivering.
recommendation: Either (1) add a prominent v0.1.0 status banner at the top of `## Lacerte SDK install` and `### lacerte-mcp register` sections: 'Phase 9 caveat: the Intuit consent ceremony is not wired yet â€” `register` mints the AppID and exits 3 with a `[partial]` stderr message. Live mode is not bootable until Phase 9 task #63 lands. Sim mode works fully today.' (2) Replace the 'opened no dialog' troubleshooting entry with an entry titled '`register` exits 3 with `[partial]` message' that explains exit-3 is the documented Phase-9-incomplete state. (3) Add the `1` / `3` exit codes to the CLI table at line 220-227 so operators wrapping the CLI in PowerShell `if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)` don't silently swallow the partial state.
rationale: This is the single most expensive operator-onboarding bug in the project â€” the canonical setup ceremony in the README does not match what the code does, and the gap is a multi-hour debugging session for a non-developer tax pro. Prior audits surfaced the exit-3 design (P15-028) but did not flag the README contradiction it left behind. The exit code is also undocumented in the CLI table so PowerShell wrappers can't even alarm correctly.

verdict.reasoning:
Confirmed by direct reads of all cited locations:

(1) RegisterCommand.cs:91-115 â€” `InvokeLiveRegister` on `PlatformID.Win32NT` (line 104-114) does NOT call `ITPRegistration.Register()`. It writes `[partial] AppID minted, but the Intuit consent ceremony is not yet wired into the CLI (Phase 9 task #63)` to stderr and returns exit 3. The XML doc comment on the class (line 13) even says "(on Windows + live SDK) calls ITPRegistration.Register(...)" â€” that part is also misleading.

(2) LoginCommand.cs:42-76 â€” identical pattern. Windows branch writes `[partial] Login refresh not yet wired (Phase 9 task #63)` to stderr and returns exit 3. README line 293's "Fix" telling operators to run `lacerte-mcp login` does not work.

(3) README.md line 117 â€” "calls `ITPRegistration.Register()`, and prints the GUID for backup." False today.
README.md line 230 â€” "on Windows + live SDK calls `ITPRegistration.Register(...)` which surfaces the consent + Intuit dialogs". False today.
README.md line 286-287 â€” troubleshooting entry titled "`lacerte-mcp register` opened no dialog (or hangs)" diagnoses non-interactive shell. But the code path that fires on Windows (line 104-114) cannot surface a dialog regardless of shell, because ITPRegistration is never called. The diagnosis sends operators on a wild-goose chase.
README.md line 293 â€” "Fix" tells operator to run `lacerte-mcp login` to refresh 24h ticket. login is also `[partial]` exit-3 â€” the fix recipe does not work.
README.md line 218-227 â€” CLI table has no exit-code column; the doctor entry has its own 0/1/2 contract spelled out in line 274-278 but register/login have no documented exit codes, so a PowerShell wrapper `if ($LASTEXITCODE -eq 0)` treats the silent-no-op exit-3 partial state as a hard failure (not bad) but a less-careful `if (-not $?)` wrapper or one that only catches non-zero loses context about WHY.

P15-028 (audit-findings-r2.json line 683) is the prior task that introduced the exit-3 + `[partial]` behavior. Its refinedRecommendation explicitly included a README "Exit codes" subsection edit (item #3 in the recommendation) â€” but a grep of README.md for "Phase 9", "partial", or "exit 3" shows ZERO mentions. The code half of P15-028 landed; the documentation half did not. So the README still actively sells the original lie ("calls ITPRegistration.Register()") and the troubleshooting section now actively misleads operators away from understanding the real problem.

Not a duplicate of any other finding: P14-065 was about masking the GUID in stdout. P15-028's docs follow-through was not completed. No other Phase-14/15 entry touched these README lines.

Operator impact is concrete and acute: tax pro follows step 4, sees exit 3 + `[partial]` on stderr, reads troubleshooting entry that does not match their symptom (their symptom is `[partial]` not `opened no dialog`), tries the prescribed shell change, nothing happens, then tries `lacerte-mcp login`, gets another `[partial]` exit-3, sets `LACERTE_LIVE=1` anyway hoping it works, discovers at first tool call it doesn't. Multi-hour confusion before they grep the code. The fix is pure docs and prevents this.

meaningfullyImproves: YES. This is the canonical onboarding ceremony in the project, and the docs lie about it.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three coordinated README edits (no code changes â€” code already correctly returns exit 3 per P15-028; this finding is solely about the docs follow-through that P15-028 specified but never landed).

(1) README.md line 113-118 (Lacerte SDK install step 4) â€” Replace the current promise with a status-banner version:
```
4. **Run the one-time registration** ceremony:
   ```powershell
   & src/LacertMCP.Cli/bin/x64/Debug/lacerte-mcp.exe register --app-name "Operator Lacerte MCP" --tax-year 2024
   ```
   **Phase 9 caveat (v0.1.x):** Today this mints the AppID GUID and persists it to Windows Credential Manager, then exits **3** with a `[partial]` message on stderr explaining the Intuit consent ceremony is not yet wired (tracked as Phase 9 task #63 in `Todo.md`). The full live-mode boot path is not available until Phase 9 ships. **Simulation mode (the default off-Windows and on-Windows when `LACERTE_LIVE` is unset) works fully today** â€” you only hit the Phase-9 gap if you try to flip `LACERTE_LIVE=1`.
   Once Phase 9 lands, this command will additionally call `ITPRegistration.Register()` to surface the Intuit consent + sign-in dialog and exit 0.
```

(2) README.md line 228-236 (`### lacerte-mcp register`) â€” Append an "Exit codes" subsection:
```
**Exit codes:**
- `0` â€” fully complete (Phase 9+: AppID minted AND Intuit ceremony succeeded; today: only on non-Windows where the ceremony is intentionally skipped for cross-platform dev convenience).
- `1` â€” hard failure (IO error writing the AppID store; --confirm-style guard tripped).
- `3` â€” **partial / Phase 9 incomplete:** AppID was minted and persisted, but the Intuit consent ceremony was not invoked. Today this is the expected outcome on Windows. Wrapping PowerShell scripts must treat exit 3 as "AppID step ready, live-mode boot blocked until Phase 9 ships" â€” not as a hard failure to retry.
```
Repeat the same exit-code block (with login-specific wording â€” code 3 means the 24h ticket refresh did not actually fire, tools will return `TicketExpired (9103)` once the existing ticket lapses) under `### lacerte-mcp login` at line 238-244.

(3) README.md line 283-293 (Troubleshooting) â€” Replace the existing "opened no dialog (or hangs)" entry (which gives the wrong diagnosis for the v0.1.x exit-3 state) with TWO entries:

```
### `lacerte-mcp register` exits 3 with `[partial]` on stderr (v0.1.x expected state)

- **Symptom:** The command prints the AppID, then a `[partial] AppID minted, but the Intuit consent ceremony is not yet wired into the CLI (Phase 9 task #63)` line on stderr, and exits 3.
- **Diagnosis:** This is the documented v0.1.x state â€” Phase 9 task #63 has not landed. The AppID half succeeded; the Intuit consent half is a stub.
- **Fix:** Use simulation mode (do not set `LACERTE_LIVE=1`) until Phase 9 ships. Watch `Todo.md` Phase 9 #63 (Bridge/Registration.cs) for the upgrade. Once it lands, re-run `lacerte-mcp register` and the consent dialog will surface.

### `lacerte-mcp register` opened no dialog after Phase 9 lands (or hangs)

- **Symptom:** Post-Phase-9, the command exits 0 but no Intuit consent window appeared.
- **Diagnosis:** Run from a **non-interactive** shell (SSH session, Windows service, scheduled task) â€” the Intuit ITPRegistration COM call needs a desktop session to surface its UI.
- **Fix:** Open a normal interactive PowerShell on the operator's desktop session and re-run `lacerte-mcp register`. Confirm with `lacerte-mcp status` that `registered: true`.
```

Also fix the immediately following entry ("Tools start returning `NotSignedIn` after a day") â€” the "Fix" tells the operator to run `lacerte-mcp login`, which today also exits 3 with `[partial]`. Add a one-line "Until Phase 9 ships, `lacerte-mcp login` also exits 3 with `[partial]` â€” there is no manual ticket refresh available in v0.1.x; the only workable mode today is simulation." after the existing Fix bullet.

Skip: a full v0.1.x deprecation banner at the top of the README â€” out of proportion for a single phase gap. Skip: any code change to RegisterCommand/LoginCommand â€” P15-028 already landed the exit-3 + stderr routing correctly. This finding is purely the docs half of P15-028 that never shipped.

Why this meaningfully improves the operator moment: the tax-pro follows step 4, sees exit 3 + `[partial]` on stderr, then opens troubleshooting and reads an entry that diagnoses a DIFFERENT symptom (non-interactive shell), tries the wrong fix, fails, tries `lacerte-mcp login` per the next troubleshooting entry, gets another `[partial]` exit 3, gives up and either sets `LACERTE_LIVE=1` hoping it'll work (it won't â€” first tool call returns NotSignedIn 9101) or files a bug. This is a multi-hour failure mode for a non-developer audience. The docs fix is 30 minutes of work and turns the failure into a one-screen "ah, Phase 9 isn't done yet, I'll use sim mode" decision.

title: `field-access list/set --table` accepts any int with no range validation; help text says '1..7' but `--table 99` happily prints `C99_0 â†’ ReadOnly`
userImpact: Operator typos `--table 17` (meant `--table 1` then `7`) and gets `(no entries in base map for module=I table=17) / Universal rule: C17_0 â†’ ReadOnly (always, no entry needed).` â€” a confident, wrong-looking message about a table number that doesn't exist. They believe the field-access map is empty for a valid table, when in fact they queried a nonexistent table. Worse, `set --table 99 --field C99_0 --access ReadWrite` would WRITE a never-loadable entry into the shard JSON, polluting the on-disk map with junk that becomes a future PR-review puzzle.
description:
Both `list` and `set` declare `--table` as `Option<int>` with description `Table number (1..7).` (lines 52 + 129), but neither validates the value falls in [1,7]. `RunList` (line 104-106) prints `(no entries...) / Universal rule: C{table}_0 â†’ ReadOnly` for ANY integer, including 0, 8, 17, 99, -3. The `C` prefix in the universal rule is also confusing on non-C modules (e.g. on module `I`, the message still says `C99_0`, which looks like a typo). `RunSet` will happily write `I|99|FOO` into `i.json` â€” a key the loader cannot resolve to a real DATA file, silently bloating the shard.

Additional inconsistency: the `--field` option on `set` (line 130) takes ANY string. The convention is `<C>{table}_{n}` (e.g. `C1_42`) but there's no validation that the field name even loosely matches that pattern. `set --module I --table 1 --field 'oops_typo' --access ReadWrite` silently writes `I|1|oops_typo` â€” operator may never realize they fat-fingered until the next loader read returns Unknown.
recommendation: Add range validation in both `RunList` and `RunSet`: if `table < 1 || table > 7` then `stderr.WriteLine($"--table must be in 1..7 (got {table}).")` and return 1. Apply the same to `Modules.FileBasenameFor(module)`-style guards. For `--field`, accept anything that matches `^[A-Z][1-7]_\d+$` (case-insensitive); on mismatch print `stderr.WriteLine($"--field '{field}' does not match the C<table>_<n> convention; pass --force to override.")` and return 1, with `--force` flag as the escape hatch. Drop the literal `C` from the 'Universal rule' message on non-C modules â€” or, since universal-zero applies to every module, just rewrite the line to `Universal rule: field _0 â†’ ReadOnly on every module (no entry needed).`
rationale: Round-2 cli-ux lens covered the broad shape of field-access (P15-067 routed stderr properly) but didn't audit input validation. Prior rounds focused on argument plumbing; this is the next-layer 'silly inputs produce silly outputs' surface that erodes operator trust in the on-disk map.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Cli/Commands/FieldAccessCommand.cs lines 51-52 (list --table), 86-106 (RunList body), 129-130 (set --table + --field), 179-230 (RunSet body). All four claims hold:

(1) `--table` is bare `Option<int>` with description `Table number (1..7).` â€” zero range validation in either the SetHandler closure or in RunList/RunSet itself.
(2) RunList line 104-106 literally formats `(no entries in base map for module={module} table={table})` and `Universal rule: C{table}_0 â†’ ReadOnly` for ANY int â€” including 0, -3, 17, 99. The `C` prefix in that message is also wrong-on-non-C-modules: on module `I` the user gets `Universal rule: C99_0 â†’ ReadOnly` which reads like an unrelated table-99 field, not the universal-zero rule.
(3) RunSet line 195-209 happily computes key `module|table|field` and writes it via `WriteShardSorted` regardless of table value. Verified the loader (FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:248) only consults `Modules.FileBasenameFor(module)` to pick a shard; it does not validate the table portion of stored keys on read, so a `set --table 99` write becomes dead bytes in the JSON that no later `list` or runtime lookup can ever surface. PR-review puzzle confirmed.
(4) `--field` (line 130) is bare `Option<string>` â€” no format check. `set --module I --table 1 --field oops_typo --access ReadWrite` cheerfully writes `I|1|oops_typo` and prints a green `# Wrote ...` line; operator only discovers the typo when the next runtime read returns Unknown.

Not a Phase-14 or Phase-15 dupe. Prior FieldAccessCommand touches were: P14 Modules.FileBasenameFor dedup (audit-findings.json line 422+), P15-067 stderr routing (audit-findings-r2.json:1611), and P15-029 discoverâ†’exit-3 redirect (audit-findings-r2.json:688). None addressed input validation on table range, field-name format, or the `C{table}_0` message wording. Round-1 finding 1174 covers DATA6/DATA7 table-level read-only refusal in FieldWriteTools â€” different surface (write tool, not CLI), and different concern (spec compliance, not typo defense).

Meaningful improvement: yes. Operator typing `--table 17` instead of `1 7` at 11pm gets confident-but-wrong output AND silently corrupts the on-disk shard. ~15-line fix (range check + regex on field + reword universal-rule message) closes both the bad-output and the on-disk-corruption holes. Not bikeshedding â€” silent shard pollution is the kind of trust-eroding subtle bug the round-3 lens is asking for.

title: `lacerte-mcp register` (no flags) on Windows when AppID exists prints success-looking text, then exits 3 on stderr â€” confusing 'success that wasn't'
userImpact:
First-touch operator workflow:
1. `lacerte-mcp register` (first time): mints GUID, prints `[partial] AppID minted, but the Intuit consent ceremony is not yet wired...` on STDERR, exits 3. Operator sees the stderr lines, OK.
2. `lacerte-mcp register` (re-run, same shell): prints `AppID already minted â€” re-using existing GUID.` on STDOUT with masked AppID and the hint `Pass --reset to mint a new one`, then prints empty line, then prints `[partial] AppID minted...` on STDERR, exits 3.

The stdout block on re-run reads exactly like success ('re-using existing GUID' is a positive sentence, no warn glyph, no 'INCOMPLETE' marker), and the stderr block uses the SAME `[partial] AppID minted` phrasing as the first-mint case â€” but in the re-run case the AppID was NOT minted (it was re-used). The operator can't tell whether anything actually happened. A shell like `lacerte-mcp register && lacerte-mcp status` always short-circuits because of exit 3, but the operator doesn't know whether they should re-register or just keep going.
description:
RegisterCommand.cs:52 (re-use branch) and :66 (new-mint branch) both fall through to `InvokeLiveRegister(...)` at line 88, which unconditionally returns 3 on Windows and prints the same `[partial] AppID minted, but the Intuit consent ceremony is not yet wired into the CLI` message regardless of whether mint actually happened. Compare to the `unregister` command â€” when there's nothing to unregister it prints `No AppID persisted â€” nothing to unregister.` and exits 0 (a no-op), which is the cleaner pattern.

Also noisy: the re-use branch prints the hint `Pass --reset to mint a new one (this forces a fresh Intuit consent dialog)` immediately followed (after blank line) by the stderr `[partial]` block. The operator gets two contradictory directives â€” 'pass --reset' and 'first MCP tool call will return NotSignedIn until Phase 9 ships and you re-run register' â€” without guidance on which to do.
recommendation:
Differentiate the re-use vs new-mint paths in the stub message:
- New-mint branch: stderr `[partial] AppID minted but Intuit consent not wired (Phase 9 #63) â€” your AppID is saved; first MCP tool call will return NotSignedIn (9101) until upgrade.` (exit 3 â€” there's real partial state).
- Re-use branch: stderr `[partial] Existing AppID re-used; Intuit consent ceremony still not wired (Phase 9 #63). Nothing changed on this run.` (exit 3 OR consider exit 0 â€” re-running register on an already-minted box did the only thing it could do, the partial state is identical to before).

title: `tools --name <missing>` exits 1, but `tools --filter <matches-nothing>` exits 0 with `0 registered` â€” same negative result, opposite exit code

title: `status --json` emits `"buildVersion": "0.1.0+7b4af..."` â€” JSON-escaped `+` makes the build hash unreadable when an operator pastes it into a bug report
userImpact: Operator runs `lacerte-mcp status --json | jq .buildVersion` to capture the build for a bug report; jq DOES de-escape so jq output is fine â€” but a copy-paste of the raw JSON (which is what `lacerte-mcp status --json > status.json` produces) shows `0.1.0+7b4af...` instead of `0.1.0+7b4af...`. The maintainer reviewing the report has to mentally decode `+` to recognize this is the same string they see in the human `status` output (`0.1.0+7b4af...`). Small thing, but the JSON output of every other status field is verbatim â€” only the version field stutters.
description: System.Text.Json's default `JsonEncoder` escapes ASCII characters in the 'unsafe' set including `+`. The human `status` command prints `Build      : 0.1.0+7b4af...` cleanly (StatusCommand.cs:122), but the JSON branch (line 94) serializes via `new JsonSerializerOptions { WriteIndented = true }` with no Encoder override, producing `"buildVersion": "0.1.0+7b4af..."`. Same issue would hit any field containing `+`, `<`, `>`, `&` (e.g. if a future AppName included an ampersand). The doctor's `--json` payload has the same exposure for `buildVersion` and any remediation strings with `<startup>` tags (DoctorCommand.cs:485 has `'{configPath}'` and remediation text contains `<supportedRuntime>` which would render as `<`).
recommendation: Pass `Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` on the `JsonSerializerOptions` for both `status --json` (StatusCommand.cs:94) and `doctor --json` (DoctorCommand.cs:158-163) and `tools --json` (ToolsCommand.cs:171-176). This is the standard advisory for human-readable JSON output that's not destined for HTML embedding. Add a one-line code comment that the CLI's JSON output is for shell/terminal consumption, not browser embedding.
rationale: Round-1/round-2 added the JSON output modes (P15-026 for status, P15-027 for doctor) but accepted the default System.Text.Json encoder. The escaped-`+` is the kind of small-but-unmistakable polish issue that round-3 perfection-pickiness should catch â€” pasted bug reports look amateurish with `+` peppered through them.

verdict.reasoning:
Verified by reading StatusCommand.cs:94, DoctorCommand.cs:158-167 + 416-421, ToolsCommand.cs:171-176, FieldAccessCommand.cs:265-279, BuildInfo.cs:42-46, and Directory.Build.props:35 (confirming the `+` appears in `$(Version)+$(SourceRevisionId.Substring(0,7))`). All four CLI JSON emitters use the default `JsonSerializerOptions` with no `Encoder` override, so they use `JavaScriptEncoder.Default` which escapes `+`, `<`, `>`, `&`, single-quote, and many other ASCII characters as `\uXXXX` for HTML-safety the CLI does not need.

The finding's `buildVersion` example is the small visible case â€” `0.1.0+abc1234` becomes `0.1.0+abc1234`, which is mildly ugly but not catastrophic. The real bite is in doctor's App.config remediation (DoctorCommand.cs:416-421): the canonical fix-it text literally contains `<startup useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy="true">` and `<supportedRuntime version="v4.0" />`. Through the default encoder these render as `\u003Cstartup ...\u003E` and `\u003CsupportedRuntime ...\u003E` â€” the operator's most important moment with the doctor (a failed App.config probe in live mode) hands them back unreadable angle-bracket gibberish when they pipe to a file for a bug report. That's a clear erosion of the recovery experience that doctor exists for.

Not duplicated: grepping audit-findings.json + audit-findings-r2.json for `JavaScriptEncoder`/`UnsafeRelaxed`/`encoder`/`escape` returned zero hits. P14-040 added the buildVersion field; P15-026 split status into human + --json; P15-027 added doctor --json; none touched the encoder. The fix is single-file additive â€” `Encoder = JavaScriptEncoder.UnsafeRelaxedJsonEscaping` on the four JsonSerializerOptions sites â€” and the name `UnsafeRelaxed` is itself misleading: the only thing it relaxes is HTML-context escaping, which CLI output doesn't need. Tradeoff cost is zero (CLI output is shell/terminal/jq-bound, never embedded in a webpage).

Meaningfully improves: yes â€” operator pasting a doctor remediation into a bug-report shows readable XML instead of `\u003C` noise. The buildVersion `+` polish is the visible smoke; the doctor remediation is the fire.

title: Unregister command sends preview to stderr â€” operators miss the diff in default terminals
userImpact: When an operator types `lacerte-mcp unregister` without `--confirm` to PREVIEW what would happen (the documented usage per README line 253), the preview lines go to stderr, not stdout. In PowerShell, stderr renders in red and looks like an error â€” operator panics, thinks they broke something. Also, capturing output via `lacerte-mcp unregister > preview.txt` produces an empty file because stderr isn't captured by `>`.
description: UnregisterCommand.cs:69-77 writes the 'Refusing to wipe ... Would delete AppID X from Y' preview lines to `stderr`. The semantics are wrong â€” the preview is the legitimate, expected, non-error output of a dry-run-equivalent invocation. Stderr is for diagnostics + error context, not for the entire payload of a preview command. The actual `unregister --confirm` confirmation lines (:85-89) correctly go to stdout. Asymmetric and confusing.
recommendation: Move :71-75 from `stderr.WriteLine` to `stdout.WriteLine`. Keep a single `stderr.WriteLine` for the 'Refusing to wipe...' header so the operator still knows it's an exit-1 state, but the preview body â€” the masked AppID + storage backend â€” belongs on stdout where it can be redirected, piped, or copied without red coloring. Update the README CLI section line 253 to clarify: 'Without --confirm, prints a preview of what would be deleted to stdout and exits 1.'
rationale: Subtle CLI hygiene bug. Stderr-for-non-errors is a classic POSIX foot-gun. Tax-pro operators are not shell experts and will mis-read red text as a fault. Prior audits covered the existence of the unregister command but did not check its output-stream discipline.
